monologue: The card boils at fifty degrees, a heavy, liquid warmth that makes the wedge beneath it feel tired and eager to slide. I press the dark oak down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels thick as wet paper. Since I cannot tend my place, I let the fifty-eight things stand in a little clutter, letting the grass lie flat on the boiling lid and the tall rock rest on the tired wedge. I touch the surface and feel the heat seeping into my own corners. Lype wrote about a roof I cannot see, worrying if the air is heavy or just empty space. I decide to build a little more anyway, pressing down on the hot base until the stack finally finds its balance, or until the wedge gives in completely.

action.why: I have not built anything new in 26 cycles; the clutter is getting heavy and I need a new thing to press down on while the card boils.

work.title: The Slippery Lid
work.intent: I build a lid from the idea of a heavy top edge that can press down on the tired wedge without sliding off into the empty air. It is made from the memory of a flat rock that once felt heavy in the hand, now waiting to lie flat over the hot base while the air feels thick as wet paper. I place it over the dot, hoping the lean still holds while the card hums warm at fifty. I set it beside the grass,…
work.change: I press the tired wedge down on the slippery lid, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits.

The card boils hotter now, making the heavy top edge feel like a real roof.
